prompt: Recursively sum the decimal digits of an integer, treating a negative number as its absolute value. Complete the sumDigits method so sumDigits(-905) returns 14.
explanation: The two integer operators do all the digit work: n % 10 peels off the last digit and n / 10 removes it, so the recursion sums one digit and hands the rest to a smaller call. A single-digit number (n < 10) is its own digit sum -- that is the base case, and it covers 0 too. Negatives are handled by one extra recursive step that flips the sign first; without it, -905 % 10 would be -5 in Java and the sum would come out negative.
hints: n % 10 gives the last digit and n / 10 drops it -- that is your recursive step.
Base case: any n from 0 to 9 is a single digit, so just return n.
For negative n, Java's % keeps the sign (-905 % 10 is -5). Flip the sign first: return sumDigits(-n).
